overview.headline: Earth atmosphere thins with altitude across three model zones

keyPoints.point: Gravity holds the thin atmosphere to the surface of Earth
keyPoints.quote: Gravity holds the atmosphere to the Earth’s surface.

keyPoints.point: Air temperature is highest near the surface and decreases as altitude increases
keyPoints.quote: Thus the air temperature is highest near the surface and decreases as altitude increases.

keyPoints.point: Air pressure decreases as altitude increases because less air remains above
keyPoints.quote: Therefore, air pressure decreases as we increase altitude.

keyPoints.point: Standard model uses three separate zones for troposphere and stratosphere layers
keyPoints.quote: The model has three zones with separate curve fits for the troposphere, the lower stratosphere, and the upper stratosphere.

keyTerms.gloss: Thin layer of air forming the atmosphere above the surface
keyTerms.quote: Gravity holds the atmosphere to the Earth’s surface.

keyTerms.gloss: Rate describing temperature decrease with height
keyTerms.quote: The rate of temperature decrease is called the lapse rate.

keyTerms.gloss: Lowest atmospheric zone extending from the surface upward
keyTerms.quote: The troposphere runs from the surface of the Earth to 36,152 feet.
